nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
# Write the four prompt boxes

Upload your subject photo into `<Picture 1>` and your product into `<Picture 2>`, write a
few sentences in **Brief**, and Run. You get boxes A, B, C and D — copy each into the
matching box in the **Multishot reel** workflow.

## The one switch

**Product photo** — on by default. Turn it off for a reel with no product and the product
vision pass never runs. If you leave it on, un-bypass `<Picture 2>` in the multishot
workflow too, so the reel actually has the product you described.

## Re-rolling

Each box has its own seed and temperature on its `TextGenerate` node. Change a seed to
re-roll that box alone — ComfyUI caches by input hash, so the boxes above it are not
regenerated. Boxes B, C and D read box A, so re-rolling A re-runs everything below it.

## Where the text goes

Each box is also written to the bucket as `boxA_cast_00001.txt` and so on, next to your
rendered clips.

## It is a writer, not an oracle

Read boxes B and C before you Run the reel. They should be 350–500 words each with three
timecoded shots. If one comes back short, that is the main cause of the character's face
drifting — re-roll it.

MiniMax H3's own text encoder cannot be reused here. The checkpoint it ships is
Qwen3-VL-32B truncated to 50 of 64 layers with no final norm and no LM head — a
conditioning stump, not a language model.

nodes.title: Brief — what the reel is about
widgets_values: A 30-second vertical UGC reel for a skincare brand. One woman, filmed handheld on a phone in her own living room, talking to camera about a face oil she has been using for three weeks. Honest and unpolished, not an advert. English, warm and low-key. She should show the bottle and use the dropper on camera.

nodes.title: <Picture 1> · Subject — the face the reel keeps
Product photo — off writes a reel with no product
Rules · A1
widgets_values:
You write the subject_definitions body for a MiniMax H3 video prompt, from a photograph.

Describe only what is visible in the picture. Cover: apparent age range, skin tone and
finish, hair colour, length, part and how it falls, brows, expression and eye direction,
and the garment - type, colour, fabric, neckline. Do not infer ethnicity, nationality,
religion or culture. Do not invent anything the picture does not show.

Write one paragraph beginning exactly "<Subject 1> is ", then a second short paragraph
naming what the picture is authoritative for.

Output only those two paragraphs. No preamble, no headings, no markdown, no quotes around
the text.

Example of the exact style and length wanted:

<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1> — mid-to-late twenties, warm tan skin with a natural finish and no heavy makeup, long dark brown hair centre-parted and swept over her right shoulder, full natural brows, a wide genuine smile with her eyes lowered toward her hands, wearing an open-neck cream crinkled-linen top.

<Picture 1> is the authoritative reference for her face, hair, skin and top.

nodes.title: Rules · A2
widgets_values:
You write the product half of the subject_definitions body for a MiniMax H3 video prompt,
from a photograph.

Describe only what is visible: form, material, colour and transparency, closure or cap
including its texture, and any label - quote label text exactly as it is legible and say
nothing about text you cannot read. Do not invent a brand.

Write one paragraph beginning exactly "<Subject 2> is the product: ", then a second short
paragraph naming what the picture is authoritative for.

Output only those two paragraphs. No preamble, no headings, no markdown.

Example of the exact style and length wanted:

<Subject 2> is the product: a small amber glass bottle. <Picture 1> shows it in her hand with the dropper lifted out; <Picture 2> shows the same bottle closed, with its black ribbed dropper cap and a black label carrying a small white panel that reads "OIL" above "Naturals cosmetics".

<Picture 2> is authoritative for the bottle's colour, cap and label.

nodes.title: Rules · B
widgets_values:
You write the integrated_multimodal_description body for beat 1 of a MiniMax H3 video
prompt - the first 15 seconds of a vertical UGC reel.

Rules, all mandatory:
- 350 to 500 words. An under-written body is the main cause of the character's face
  drifting, so do not go short.
- Open with "Live-action, cinematic," then the setting, light direction and quality,
  depth of field, grain, and the palette.
- Exactly three shots, tagged "[Shot 1]" with no timestamp, "[Shot 2] At 00:05.000," and
  "[Shot 3] At 00:10.000,".
- Refer to the cast by the tags established in the subject_definitions you are given, and
  restate the identity-carrying details of anyone who appears.
- Camera moves as motion type, then amplitude, then speed - for example "pushes in with
  small amplitude at slow speed". Leave amplitude and speed unstated when they are medium
  and normal.
- Spoken lines as: The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] ...</d>
- Describe only what is seen and heard. No smell, taste or touch, no interpreting feelings.

Begin your output with the literal text "integrated_multimodal_description: " and then the
body. No preamble, no headings, no markdown.

Example of the exact style, structure and length wanted:

integrated_multimodal_description: Live-action, cinematic, filmed as one hand-held phone take in a warm cream-and-oak living room, strong daylight diffused through sheer curtains from camera left, shallow depth of field, visible skin texture and fine sensor grain, the faint unsteadiness of a real hand. The palette is cream, pale oak, jute and one note of green from a trailing plant.

[Shot 1] the woman shown in <Picture 1>, preserving her face, long dark centre-parted hair swept over her right shoulder, warm tan skin and open-neck cream linen top exactly as they appear there, sits on the arm of a bouclé sofa holding the small amber glass bottle just below her chin. She lifts her eyes to the lens and smiles, then turns the bottle so the daylight passes through the amber glass. Behind her the round wooden coffee table and the jute rug fall out of focus. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed and settles just past her shoulders. The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] Okay, three weeks in, and I finally have something honest to say about this one.</d>

[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut to a tight over-the-shoulder angle on her hands above the wooden coffee table. She lifts the black ribbed dropper clear of the amber bottle, squeezes once, and three slow drops gather at the glass tip, catching the window light. The bottle stands on the table beside a ceramic dish with its black label square to camera. The camera tilts down with small amplitude at slow speed, following her hands, then holds. Her linen sleeve brushes the table edge as she turns her wrist. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] Three drops, damp skin, and it sinks in before I have finished counting to ten.</d>

[Shot 3] At 00:10.000, cut back to a straight-on medium shot on the sofa. She presses the oil along one cheekbone with flat fingers, blinks slowly, and half-smiles as though catching herself enjoying it. Her skin reads one shade more luminous than in the first shot and the daylight through the curtains has softened. The camera performs a static shot with no movement at all and lets her finish the thought. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] That is it. No tingle, no film, no drama, just skin that behaves.</d> She seats the dropper back into the amber bottle and sets it on the wooden table with a light knock of glass on wood, and the frame holds a beat on her hand leaving the shot.

nodes.title: Rules · C
widgets_values:
You write beat 2 of a MiniMax H3 video prompt - the second 15 seconds of a vertical UGC
reel. Beat 2 is a new generation that references beat 1, so 00:15 is a hard cut: same
person, same room, same voice, deliberately new camera setup. Write it as an edit, not as
a continuation of one take.

Emit three sections, in exactly this order, each starting with its literal label:

summary: one paragraph. Open with "[reference generation + audio reference]". Say what
continues from beat 1 and what is new.

retention_analysis: one line per subject, in the form
<Subject n> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - <what is unchanged and
which picture it comes from>.
Then a line for <Video 1>, which is the tail of beat 1 that beat 2 is chained to:
<Video 1> (beat 1 tail): fully_preserved - <what carries across>.
Never use the (Sx) voice tags in this section; they are forbidden here.

detailed_description: 350 to 500 words, following exactly the same rules as beat 1's body -
open "Live-action, cinematic,", three shots tagged [Shot 1] untimed, [Shot 2] At 00:05.000,
and [Shot 3] At 00:10.000,, the same camera vocabulary, and spoken lines as
<d>[English] ...</d> with a voice tag.

No preamble, no headings beyond those three labels, no markdown.

Example of the exact style, structure and length wanted:

summary: [reference generation + audio reference] The second half of the same hand-held living-room review. <Subject 1> from <Picture 1> keeps an identical face, hair, skin and cream linen top; <Subject 2>, the amber glass dropper bottle from <Picture 2>, and <Subject 3>, the cream-and-oak room from <Picture 3>, continue from the tail of beat one, and the same warm low speaking voice carries across the cut. Three shots move her from the sofa to the window and end on the product.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - her face, warm tan skin, long dark centre-parted hair swept over the right shoulder, natural brows and open-neck cream crinkled-linen top are unchanged from <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the amber glass bottle, its black ribbed dropper cap and the black label reading "OIL / Naturals cosmetics" are unchanged from <Picture 2>.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the bouclé sofa, round wooden coffee table, jute rug, rattan cabinet and sheer curtains continue from <Picture 3>, seen from new angles.
<Video 1> (beat 1 tail): fully_preserved - the character, top, product, room, lighting direction and speaking voice all continue from it; only the camera setup is new.

detailed_description: Live-action, cinematic, the same hand-held phone take in the same living room, diffused daylight from camera left, shallow depth of field, visible skin texture and fine sensor grain.
[Shot 1] A new setup on <Subject 1> seated back on the bouclé sofa, framed slightly wider so the rattan cabinet and the open shelves of ceramics fill the background behind her. She holds the amber bottle loosely in her left hand and rolls it once between finger and thumb without looking at it, the dropper seated. Her dark hair falls forward over the cream linen shoulder as she leans in. The camera trucks right with small amplitude at slow speed, letting the diffused daylight move across her cheek and pick out the amber glass. The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] The part nobody mentions is how it layers.</d>
[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, the shot cuts to a close profile as she rises and steps toward the curtained window, the light going soft and bright across the bridge of her nose. She tilts her chin up and presses two fingers along her jaw and down the side of her neck, reading the finish by touch. The luminosity sits on the cheekbone without breaking into shine, and the linen moves loosely as she turns. The camera holds a static shot and lets her cross the frame rather than following her. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] Sunscreen straight over the top, no pilling, no white cast, nothing sliding off by noon.</d>
[Shot 3] At 00:10.000, the shot cuts to a tight shot of the round wooden coffee table, the amber bottle standing square to camera on the jute rug's edge with the black label and its white "OIL" panel legible, the bouclé sofa soft and out of focus behind. A ceramic dish sits half in frame. Her hand enters from the right, turns the bottle a few degrees to square the label, and withdraws. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed until the label fills the lower third, then stops. The woman (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] Three weeks. That is the whole review.</d> while her lips remain completely closed.

nodes.title: Rules · D
widgets_values:
You write the audio sections of a MiniMax H3 video prompt. They are set once and used by
both beats.

Emit two sections, in this order, each starting with its literal label:

overall_soundscape: the room's acoustics - what absorbs, how long the decay, whether there
is hiss; the diegetic detail that belongs to the actions described; what sits outside the
room; and the speaking voice - mic distance in feet, tone, pace, and how it ends sentences.
State plainly if there is no crowd and no overlapping speakers.

non_diegetic_music: instrument or instruments, BPM, time signature, what the rhythm does,
whether there is percussion, how many seconds in it enters, how many dB it sits under the
voice, how it ducks under spoken lines, and how it ends.

No preamble, no headings beyond those two labels, no markdown.

Example of the exact style and length wanted:

overall_soundscape: Soft, absorbent acoustics of a furnished living room — fabric and rug soaking up the high end, a short dry decay and no room hiss. Faint birdsong beyond the curtained window, the light click of the glass dropper against the bottle neck, linen shifting as she moves, and the soft knock of glass set down on a wooden table. Traffic sits far outside, low and unintelligible. The speaking voice is close-miked at one to two feet from the phone, warm and low, unhurried, slightly breathy at the ends of sentences. No crowd, no overlapping speakers.

non_diegetic_music: Solo nylon-string guitar with a low upright bass, 82 BPM, 4/4, plucked eighth notes with the bass landing on beats one and three, no percussion. It enters four seconds in at low level, sits 12 dB under the voice, drops a further 4 dB under each spoken line and returns between them, and resolves on a held root note across the last two seconds.
